  6. Location:

    1. "Can you let me know which county this matter is in?"

        1. Calvert

    The transfer is not the consultation itself, but for the attorney to learn about their case and consultation scheduling.

    1. "Before I connect you, I want to let you know this will be a brief call with the attorney to go over your situation. If you decide to move forward after speaking with her, the consultation fee is $150. Are you okay with that?"

      1. If Yes

        1. Checking office hours...

          Initiate Warm Transfer to Valerie

          1. "Thank you for everything. Let me get this over to Attorney Desroches and see if she's available now."

            1. Briefing Valerie

              1. "Hi Valerie, I have a new client on the line who is okay with the $150 consultation fee - his/her name is [First and Last Name] on the line and calling from [County] regarding:"

                1. [Family/Criminal/Personal Injury] matter

                2. There are [X] children involved

                3. He/she was served / looking to initiate

                4. And he/she has an upcoming court case on [Date] / has no upcoming court dates

                5. "Can I patch you through?"

            1. If Not Available

              1. "They're not available right now, but I can take a message and have them get back to you by the end of today."

      2. If No

        1. Do Not Warm Transfer - Take Message

          1. "Thank you for everything. I have everything noted down here and she'll get back to you by the end of today. Is there anything else I can help you with?"

            1. Closing

              1. "Thank you for entrusting us with your legal matter."

Legal Matter (Internal Reference)

  1. Family Immigration

    1. Green card for spouse

      1. Helping a husband or wife get permanent residence in the U.S.

    2. Green card for parent / family member

      1. U.S. citizen sponsoring their mother / father / child / sibling for a green card.

    3. Fiancé visa (K-1 visa)

      1. Bringing a fiancé(e) to the U.S. to get married.

    4. Adjustment of status

      1. Applying for a green card while already inside the U.S., instead of going through a U.S. consulate abroad.

  2. Citizenship

    1. Naturalization / citizenship application

      1. Applying to become a U.S. citizen.

  3. Business / Employment Immigration

    1. H1-B visa

      1. Work visa for foreign professionals hired by a U.S. employer.

    2. Investor visa

      1. A visa based on investing money in a U.S. business.

    3. Employment-based immigration

      1. Immigration based on a job or employer sponsorship.

  4. ICE Matters

    Trigger words: ICE, ICE detention

    1. ICE-related matters

  5. Removal Defense / Humanitarian Immigration
    Note: Only qualify and forward these cases if the individual is not currently in an immigration detention center.

    1. Removal defense / deportation defense (if not in a detention center)

    2. Asylum (if not in a detention center)

    3. Immigration Court

      1. "Is your court matter related to removal or deportation proceedings or asylum?"

        1. If Yes

          1. "Are you currently being held in an immigration detention center?"

            1. If Yes - Disqualify

            2. If No

              1. Proceed to Next Question

        2. If No - Disqualify

First Question:

Transition to Questions:

  • "Thank you, and I'll need a few quick details from you"


New Client:

  1. Full Name

    1. "May I please have your first and last name?"

      1. Ask Them To Spell

        1. "Can you please spell that out for me?"

          1. (repeat spelling if unclear)

  2. Confirm Caller Relationship (If not self-identified)

    1. "Are you calling on behalf of yourself or someone else?"

      1. Calling About Themself

        1. Proceed to Next Question

      2. Calling on Behalf of Someone Else (Subject of the Case)

        1. Full Name

          1. "May I please have their first and last name?"

        2. Ask Them To Spell

          1. "Can you please spell that out for me?"

            1. (repeat spelling if unclear)

  3. Confirm Five9 Caller ID Phone Number

    1. "If we get disconnected, is the number you're calling from ending in XXXX the best number to reach you?"

      1. If No

        1. Acquire Best Phone Number for Callback

          1. "What's your best callback number?"

  4. Email Address

    1. "Can I please have your email address?"

      1. (repeat out loud to confirm accuracy)

  5. Date of Birth

    1. If Caller is calling on behalf of themself

      1. "Can I please have your date of birth?"

        1. (repeat out loud to confirm accuracy)

    2. If Caller is calling on behalf of someone else

      1. "Can I please have their date of birth?"

        1. (repeat out loud to confirm accuracy)

  6. Legal Matter (Caller may also elaborate on their Purpose for Calling during this question)

    1. "What type of legal help are you calling about today?"

      1. Internal Reference:

        1. Personal Injury - injuries caused by negligence or accidents

          1. Motor Vehicle Accidents - injuries from car, truck, motorcycle, or rideshare accidents

          2. Premises Liability (Slip & Fall / Trip & Fall) - injuries caused by unsafe property conditions

          3. Workplace Injuries / Workers Compensation - workplace injuries and occupational illnesses sustained on the job

          4. Dog Bites - injuries from dog or animal attacks

  7. Route to the Matter Type

    1. Open the matter type below that matches the caller's legal matter and work through it there. Each one holds the rest of the call.

    2. If Motor Vehicle Accidents:

        (be kind, empathetic and understanding)

      2. Location of Incident

        1. "Can you please share the city and state the accident took place in?"

          2. If No

                1. If Returning or Referred Client:

                  1. "Just to confirm, have you worked with us before, or were you referred by one of our clients?"

                    1. If Yes
                      Not Qualified but Attorney will review if Returning or Referred Caller

                      1. "Thank you - that's very helpful. I'll share this information with our attorneys, and someone will follow up with you. Since you were not injured in the accident, we may not be able to handle your case, but the attorneys will review everything to make sure."

      4. Responsible Party

        1. "Just to clarify - do you know if the accident was caused by someone else, or were you found at fault?"

          1. Note the answer in the call summary.

Legal Practice: Bankruptcy Focus

  1. Bankruptcy / Debt Settlement - getting out from under debt, by filing or by negotiating it down

    • Chapter 7 - unsecured debt (credit cards, medical bills, personal loans) wiped out for a fresh start

    • Chapter 13 - a repayment plan over three to five years, usually to keep a house or a vehicle

    • Debt Settlement - negotiating with creditors to pay less than what is owed, without filing

    • Foreclosure Defense - stopping or delaying a foreclosure sale, or catching up on a mortgage

    • Wage Garnishment / Collections - money being taken from pay, collection calls, judgments and lawsuits over debt

    • Vehicle Repossession - a car taken, or about to be taken, over a loan

  2. Will / Estate / Probate - planning for what happens to a person's property, and handling it after they pass

    • Wills and Trusts - writing or updating a will, or setting up a trust

    • Health Care Proxy / Power of Attorney - naming someone to make medical or financial decisions

    • Probate / Estate Administration - settling a deceased person's estate through the court

    • Contested Wills - a dispute over what a will says or whether it is valid

  3. Business Disputes - disagreements involving a business

    • Contract Disputes - one side says the other broke an agreement

    • Partner / Owner Disputes - disagreements between the people who own or run a business

    • Unpaid Invoices / Collections - money a business is owed, or owes

    • Business Bankruptcy (Chapter 11) - a business reorganizing or winding down its debt

          1. "What's your best callback number?"

  4. Email Address

    1. "Can I please have your email address?"

      1. (repeat out loud to confirm accuracy)

  5. Legal Matter

    1. "Are you calling about bankruptcy, or another debt issue like collections, foreclosure, or a repossession?"

      1. Legal Matter

        • Chapter 7 - unsecured debt (credit cards, medical bills, personal loans) wiped out for a fresh start

        • Chapter 13 - a repayment plan over three to five years, usually to keep a house or a vehicle

        • Debt Settlement - negotiating with creditors to pay less than what is owed, without filing

        • Foreclosure Defense - stopping or delaying a foreclosure sale, or catching up on a mortgage

        • Wage Garnishment / Collections - money being taken from pay, collection calls, judgments and lawsuits over debt

        • Vehicle Repossession - a car taken, or about to be taken, over a loan

      2. Do not tell the caller whether the firm handles their matter. Take the details and let the attorney decide.

  6. Route to the Matter Type

    1. Open the section below that matches what the caller described, and work through it in order. Each one holds the rest of the call.

    2. If Bankruptcy (Chapter 7 or Chapter 13):

      1. It is okay if the caller is not comfortable sharing financial details. Take what they are willing to share, do not press, and note the rest as declined.

      2. Massachusetts Resident

        1. "Are you a Massachusetts resident?"

      3. Owns Property in Massachusetts

        1. "Do you own any property in Massachusetts?"

          1. If Yes

            1. Current on Mortgage

              1. "Are you current with your mortgage?"

      4. Owns Property Outside Massachusetts

        1. "Do you own any additional property outside of Massachusetts?"

      5. Unsecured Debt (Type and Amount)

        1. "Roughly what kind of unsecured debt do you have - credit cards, personal loans, that sort of thing? An estimate is fine."

      6. Vehicle Loans

        1. "Do you have any vehicle loans?"

          1. If Yes

            1. Current on Vehicle Payments

              1. "Are you current with the payments?"

      7. Enrolled in a Debt Settlement Program

        1. "Are you currently enrolled in a debt settlement program?"

      8. Lawsuits or Judgments

        1. "Are there any lawsuits or judgments against you?"

      9. Pending Court Dates or Creditor Actions

        1. "Is there anything happening on a deadline - a court date, a foreclosure sale, a garnishment, or anything else from a creditor that needs attention right away?"

          1. If Yes

            1. Date and What It Is For

              1. "What's the date, and what is it for?"

      10. Family Size (Adults / Children Under 21)

        1. "How many people are in your household - how many adults, and how many children under 21?"

      11. Approximate Family Income

        1. "And roughly what is your family's total income for the year? An estimate is fine."

          1. If they say they are the only one interested in filing, acknowledge that is okay, but explain the family income is still needed for the Means Test.

      12. Preferred Consultation Time

        1. "The office offers a free 30-minute consultation to go over your situation with an attorney. What days and times work best for you?"

          1. Note the preference and let them know the office will call to confirm the appointment.

          2. Consultation Formats:

            • In-Person: 1550 Falmouth Road, Suite 10, Centerville, Massachusetts 02632

            • Zoom

            • Phone

      13. Referral Source

        1. "And how did you hear about us today?"

      14. Closing

        1. "Thanks so much for sharing everything - I've got everything noted. Someone from our office will get back to you as soon as possible."

      15. After Call Work:

        1. Complete the form and send the call summary. Flag anything the caller was unsure about rather than guessing it.

    3. If Not Bankruptcy:

Legal Practice: Personal Injury Focus

  1. Personal Injury - injuries caused by negligence or accidents

    • Motor Vehicle Accidents - car, truck, motorcycle, rideshare, and other traffic accidents

    • Workplace Injuries / Workers Compensation - injuries that occur on the job or at work

    • Dog Bites - injuries caused by dog or animal attacks

    • Premises Liability (Slip & Fall) - injuries caused by unsafe or hazardous property conditions

  2. Medical Malpractice - injuries caused by negligence from doctors, hospitals, or other healthcare providers

  3. Whistleblower Claims - cases involving retaliation or reporting fraud, misconduct, or illegal activity

  4. Social Media Harm (Minors) - cases involving harm to minors related to social media platforms or their practices

Legal Practice: Estate Planning and Probate

  1. Estate Planning - wills, trusts, powers of attorney, healthcare directives, and other planning documents

  2. Estate Administration - probate and managing a person's estate after they pass away

  3. Real Estate - buying, selling, transferring, or resolving legal issues involving property

  4. Small Business Legal Services - starting, operating, protecting, or selling a small business


Definitions (Internal Reference):

  • Estate planning happens during a person's lifetime.

    • It involves preparing documents-such as wills, trusts, powers of attorney, and healthcare directives-to explain how their wishes and assets should be handled.

  • Estate administration happens after a person dies.

    • It involves carrying out those wishes, including probate, paying debts and taxes, managing property, and distributing assets to beneficiaries.

  • Simply put: estate planning prepares the plan; estate administration carries it out.

Legal Practices:

  1. Family Law: ~75% of New Client calls

    1. Divorce - legal guidance through separation, property division, support, and dissolution of marriage

    2. Child Custody - parenting plans, legal and physical custody, visitation, and custody modifications

    3. Spousal Support - establishing, modifying, or enforcing alimony and support obligations

    4. Child Support - establishing, modifying, or enforcing child support arrangements

    5. Prenuptial and Postnuptial Agreements - marital agreements created before or during marriage to define financial rights and responsibilities

  2. Criminal Law - criminal defense matters

  3. Business Law - business formation, contracts, disputes

  4. Civil Litigation - civil disputes and lawsuits

  5. Commercial Litigation - business and commercial disputes

  6. Employment Law - workplace and employment matters

  7. Estate Law

    1. Estate Planning - wills, trusts, powers of attorney

    2. Probate - managing a person's estate after they pass away

  8. Real Estate Law - real estate matters

                  • Free

    (IMPORTANT) Identifying Correctional Facility / Jail / Prison Calls on Recorded Line

    1. Automated message announcing this call is from jail / prison / correctional facility

      • End Call immediately

    2. Caller is calling from 1-(800) or 1-(888) number

      • Confirm whether the caller is calling from a correctional facility

        • "Just to confirm, are you currently calling from a jail or prison or correctional facility?"

          • If Yes - End Call

            • "Thank you for letting me know. Unfortunately, we're unable to continue calls from correctional facilities. Please have someone contact the office on your behalf. Thank you."

    3. Caller ID displays 'CIDNET'

      • End Call immediately

        • "Just to confirm, are you currently calling from a jail or prison or correctional facility?"

          • If Yes - End Call

            • "Thank you for letting me know. Unfortunately, we're unable to continue calls from correctional facilities. Please have someone contact the office on your behalf. Thank you."

    4. Caller announces they are calling from jail / prison / correctional facility

      • End Call

        • "Unfortunately, we're unable to continue calls from correctional facilities. Please have someone contact the office on your behalf. Thank you."

    First Question:

    • "May I know if you're an existing client or expecting to be a new client?"

    Transition to Questions:

    • "Thank you, and I'll need a few quick details from you"


    New Client:

    About 50% of calls come from family members calling on behalf of a client.

    Ryan prefers to meet with the client directly, but if the client is in jail, it's okay to schedule the consultation with the family member.

    1. Full Name

      1. "May I please have your first and last name?"

        1. Ask Them To Spell

          1. "Can you please spell that out for me?"

            1. (repeat spelling if unclear)

    2. Confirm Caller Relationship (If not self-identified)

      1. "Are you calling on behalf of yourself or someone else?"

        1. Calling About Themself

          1. Proceed to Next Question

        2. Calling on Behalf of Someone Else (Subject of the Case)

          1. Full Name

            1. "May I please have their first and last name?"

          2. Ask Them To Spell

            1. "Can you please spell that out for me?"

              1. (repeat spelling if unclear)

    3. Confirm Five9 Caller ID Phone Number

      1. "If we get disconnected, is the number you're calling from ending in XXXX the best number to reach you?"

        1. If No

          1. Acquire Best Phone Number for Callback

            1. "What's your best callback number?"

    4. Email Address

      1. "Can I please have your email address?"

    5. Date of Birth

      1. If Caller is calling on behalf of themself

        1. "Can I please have your date of birth?"

          1. (repeat out loud to confirm accuracy)

      2. If Caller is calling on behalf of someone else

        1. "Can I please have their date of birth?"

          1. (repeat out loud to confirm accuracy)

    6. Mailing Address

      1. "Can I please have your mailing address?"

        1. (repeat out loud to confirm accuracy)

    7. Charges Filed (Caller may also elaborate on their Purpose for Calling during this question)

      1. "Could you briefly tell me what's going on and what charges you might be facing?"

        1. If Caller doesn't specify charges, ask for charges filed

          1. "And what charges have been filed?"

    8. Brief Description of Incident

      1. "Just so I understand the situation, can you briefly describe what happened leading up to the charges?"

    9. Date of Incident / Charge

      1. "When did the incident occur?"

    10. Location of Incident

      1. "Could you let me know what city or county the incident happened in?"

        1. Most Common Cities / Counties Served (Internal Reference) - There might be callers who call outside of this list

          1. Potter County, Texas

          2. Randall County, Texas

          3. Carson County, Texas

          4. Armstrong County, Texas

          5. Deaf Smith County, Texas

          6. Oldham County, Texas

          7. Moore County, Texas

          8. Hutchinson County, Texas

    11. Court Date/Time:

      1. "Do you have any upcoming court dates already scheduled?"

        1. If Yes

          1. "What's the date and time?"

            1. (repeat out loud to confirm accuracy)

        2. If No

          1. Proceed to next question

    12. Referral Source

      1. "And how did you hear about us today?"

    13. Closing

      1. "Thanks so much for sharing everything - I've got everything noted. Someone from our office will get back to you as soon as they're available."
